resistor-film.does: Limits current and sets voltages in a circuit by converting electrical energy to heat.
resistor-film.principle: A resistive film or wire opposes current. The voltage follows Ohm's law, V = I × R, and the heat produced is P = I² × R.
resistor-film.polarity: No polarity. Read colour bands from the end where the bands are closer together; the tolerance band (often gold or silver) sits apart.
steps: Switch the board off, unplug it and wait for the capacitors to discharge.
Select the resistance (Ω) range.
For a reliable reading, lift one lead from the board or remove the resistor.
Touch the probes to the two leads without touching both with your fingers.
Compare the reading with the colour code or marking, allowing for the tolerance.
expect: Within tolerance of the marked value, for example 1 kΩ ±5 % reads 950 to 1050 Ω.
The reading settles quickly and does not drift.
faulty: OL (open): the resistor has burnt open.
Much higher than marked: drifted or partly burnt.
Much lower than marked: usually a parallel path in the circuit, or a damaged resistor.
resistor-film.incircuit: In circuit, other parts in parallel make the reading lower than the true value. A reading equal to or higher than the marked value can be trusted; a lower one needs the resistor lifted to confirm.
symptoms: Burnt or discoloured body, sometimes with a burning smell
Resistor too hot after a short on the board
resistor-film.example: A 10 kΩ resistor reads 6.2 kΩ in circuit and 10.1 kΩ with one lead lifted. It is good: the lower reading came from a parallel path.
resistor-film.safety: Test with the power off. Resistors near a short can be hot; let them cool.
refs: IEC 60062 (marking codes for resistors and capacitors)
Manufacturer datasheet of the exact part number for tolerance, power and temperature ratings

potentiometer-trimmer.does: Provides an adjustable resistance, or an adjustable fraction of a voltage.
potentiometer-trimmer.principle: A wiper slides along a resistive track. Between the outer pins the resistance is fixed; between the wiper and an outer pin it changes with position.
potentiometer-trimmer.polarity: No polarity. The middle pin is normally the wiper.
steps: Switch the power off.
Measure between the two outer pins to get the total resistance.
Measure wiper to one outer pin while turning slowly.
Measure wiper to the other outer pin and check the two parts add up to the total.
expect: Outer pins read the rated value within tolerance.
The wiper reading changes smoothly from near 0 Ω to the total, and the two parts add to the total.
faulty: Jumpy or noisy readings while turning: dirty or worn track.
Open reading at some positions: broken track or wiper.
Total resistance wrong: damaged track.
potentiometer-trimmer.incircuit: Parallel paths distort readings, so lift one outer pin for a reliable measurement.
potentiometer-trimmer.example: A 10 kΩ pot reads 10.1 kΩ across the outer pins, but the wiper reading jumps between 2 kΩ and 8 kΩ when turned slowly: the track is worn or dirty.
potentiometer-trimmer.safety: Do not adjust trimmers on live boards unless authorised, and use an insulated tool.
refs: Manufacturer datasheet of the exact part number for resistance law, tolerance and rotation life

ceramic-capacitor.does: Stores a small charge for decoupling, filtering and timing.
ceramic-capacitor.principle: Two conductors separated by a ceramic dielectric store energy in an electric field: Q = C × V.
apps: Decoupling next to IC supply pins
steps: Switch off and make sure no voltage remains.
Remove the capacitor or lift one lead.
Select the capacitance mode.
Touch the probes to the leads and wait for the reading to settle.
Compare with the marked value and tolerance.
expect: Close to the marked value within tolerance, often ±10 % or ±20 %.
C0G types are very close; X7R and Y5V can differ and change with voltage and temperature.
faulty: Near 0 Ω on the resistance range, or very low capacitance: shorted or cracked.
Zero capacitance: open.
ceramic-capacitor.incircuit: In circuit, parallel capacitors and resistors change the reading. A short shows as a very low resistance across a supply rail; lift one lead to confirm.
ceramic-capacitor.example: A 5 V rail reads 0.4 Ω to ground on a dead board. Lifting a 100 nF capacitor makes the reading rise to hundreds of ohms: the capacitor was shorted, often a cracked MLCC after board flexing.
ceramic-capacitor.safety: Take ESD precautions. A shorted MLCC can get hot on a powered board, so touch with care.
refs: IEC 60062 (marking codes)
Manufacturer datasheet of the exact part number for dielectric type, voltage and DC-bias behaviour

electrolytic-capacitor.does: Stores a large amount of charge for smoothing and energy storage in power supplies.
electrolytic-capacitor.principle: An oxide layer on aluminium foil is the dielectric. The thin layer gives a high capacitance in a small can, but the part must be connected the right way round.
electrolytic-capacitor.polarity: Polarised. The stripe marks the negative lead; on new through-hole parts the long lead is positive.
steps: Switch off and discharge through a suitable resistor (for example 1 kΩ), then confirm 0 V with a meter.
Remove the capacitor or lift one lead.
Select the capacitance mode and connect the probes.
Compare with the marked value.
If you have an ESR meter, check the ESR too.
expect: Capacitance near the marked value; aluminium electrolytics commonly have a wide tolerance such as ±20 %.
Low ESR for a good part.
faulty: Bulging top or leaking residue.
Capacitance much lower than marked.
High ESR (needs an ESR meter).
Short circuit.
electrolytic-capacitor.incircuit: Parallel parts change the reading. An ESR meter can often test in circuit, but confirm doubtful parts by lifting one lead.
symptoms: Supply that works cold but fails when warm
electrolytic-capacitor.example: A 1000 µF 25 V smoothing capacitor measures 420 µF and has a bulged top. Replace it with the same or higher voltage rating, correct polarity.
electrolytic-capacitor.safety: Large capacitors can hold a dangerous charge: discharge through a resistor, never with a screwdriver, and confirm with a meter. Wrong polarity or over-voltage can make them fail violently.
refs: IEC 60062 (marking codes)
Manufacturer datasheet of the exact part number for ESR, ripple current and life

rectifier-diode-1n4007-m7.does: Lets current flow one way only, so it converts AC to DC.
rectifier-diode-1n4007-m7.principle: A PN junction conducts when forward biased above about 0.6 to 0.7 V for silicon, and blocks in reverse until breakdown.
apps: Freewheeling across relay and motor coils
steps: Switch off and remove or lift one leg.
Select diode mode.
Red probe on the anode, black on the cathode: note the forward drop.
Swap the probes: note the reverse reading.
expect: Forward: about 0.5 to 0.7 V for a silicon rectifier diode.
Reverse: OL.
faulty: Both directions near 0 V: shorted.
OL both ways: open.
A low reading in reverse: leaky.
rectifier-diode-1n4007-m7.incircuit: Other paths in circuit can give a false low reading. If the reading is doubtful, lift one leg.
rectifier-diode-1n4007-m7.example: On a supply with a blown fuse, one bridge diode reads 0.02 V in both directions: it is shorted. Replace it and find why it failed, for example a shorted filter capacitor.
rectifier-diode-1n4007-m7.safety: Test with the power off. On SMPS boards the primary side is at mains potential: do not probe live.
refs: Manufacturer datasheet of the exact part number (for example 1N4007)

zener-diode.does: Holds a nearly constant voltage in reverse breakdown, as a simple reference or clamp.
zener-diode.principle: When the reverse voltage reaches the Zener voltage the diode conducts and the voltage across it stays nearly constant. A series resistor limits the current.
zener-diode.polarity: The stripe marks the cathode. In use the cathode is on the more positive side.
steps: Switch off.
In diode mode test forward like any diode.
Reverse in diode mode usually reads OL, because the meter voltage is below the Zener voltage.
To check the Zener voltage, use a current-limited supply with a series resistor (for example 1 kΩ) and measure the voltage across the diode.
expect: Forward about 0.7 V; reverse OL in diode mode.
In the powered test the voltage across the diode is close to the marked Zener voltage.
faulty: Short in both directions.
Voltage in the powered test far from the marked value.
zener-diode.incircuit: In circuit, resistors and other junctions give false readings. Measure the voltage across the Zener on a powered board instead.
zener-diode.example: A 5.1 V reference reads 3.2 V on the board and its series resistor is hot: the Zener has become leaky.
zener-diode.safety: Use a current-limited supply for the powered test; the series resistor dissipates power.
refs: Manufacturer datasheet of the exact part number

led.does: Emits light when current flows in the forward direction.
led.principle: A forward-biased PN junction releases energy as light. The colour depends on the material; the forward voltage rises from about 1.8 V for red to about 3 V for blue and white.
led.polarity: The long lead is the anode. The flat side of the case is the cathode. SMD LEDs have a cathode mark; check the datasheet.
steps: Switch off.
Select diode mode.
Red probe on the anode, black on the cathode; look for a faint glow.
Swap the probes.
If a blue or white LED stays dark, test it with a supply and series resistor.
expect: Forward: often a faint glow, with a drop of about 1.6 to 3.5 V depending on colour.
Reverse: OL.
faulty: No light and OL both ways: open, or the meter voltage is too low for that colour.
Reading near 0 V: shorted.
led.incircuit: Drivers and other parts in circuit can mislead. A lit LED in diode mode proves it works; a dark one is not conclusive on some meters.
led.example: A red indicator LED does not light on the board but glows faintly in diode mode. The LED is good, so check its series resistor and drive signal.
led.safety: High-power LEDs get hot and very bright: do not look into them.
refs: Manufacturer datasheet of the exact part number

npn-transistor-bjt.does: Uses a small base current to control a larger collector current: a switch or an amplifier.
npn-transistor-bjt.principle: Ic = β × Ib in the active region. With enough base current the transistor saturates and acts as a closed switch.
npn-transistor-bjt.polarity: The pinout depends on the type and package; always check the datasheet. For a BC547 in TO-92 with the flat face toward you, the pins read C, B, E from left to right.
steps: Switch off and lift the legs if possible.
Select diode mode.
Red on base and black on emitter: note the forward drop.
Red on base and black on collector: note the forward drop.
Reverse both: expect OL.
Check collector to emitter in both directions: expect OL.
expect: About 0.6 to 0.7 V for each forward junction; higher (about 1.2 V or more) for a Darlington.
OL in reverse and between collector and emitter.
faulty: Low reading between collector and emitter: shorted.
OL on a junction that should conduct: open.
npn-transistor-bjt.incircuit: Resistors and other junctions give false readings in circuit. Lift legs, or compare with a known good board.
symptoms: Relay or load always on or never on
npn-transistor-bjt.example: A relay driver transistor reads 0.2 V collector to emitter in both directions: it is shorted, so the relay is always energised.
npn-transistor-bjt.safety: Take ESD precautions. A faulty circuit can make the transistor hot.
refs: Manufacturer datasheet of the exact part number

n-channel-mosfet.does: A voltage-controlled switch used in power supplies and drivers.
n-channel-mosfet.principle: A gate voltage creates a conducting channel between drain and source. The gate is insulated, so it draws no steady current but is easily damaged by static.
n-channel-mosfet.polarity: Pins are gate, drain and source, and the pinout varies, so check the datasheet. The tab of a TO-220 is usually the drain.
steps: Switch off. Discharge the gate by shorting gate to source.
Diode mode: red on source and black on drain should read about 0.4 to 0.7 V (the body diode).
Reverse: OL.
Gate to the other pins: OL.
Optional turn-on check: with the meter across drain and source, briefly touch the gate with the red probe, then short gate to source to turn it off.
expect: Body diode about 0.4 to 0.7 V one way and OL the other.
Drain to source is low only while the gate is charged (standard types).
faulty: Near 0 Ω between any pins: shorted.
A reading between gate and other pins: gate leakage or damage.
n-channel-mosfet.incircuit: Hard to test in circuit because of parallel paths. Measure drain to source to look for a short, then confirm on a lifted device.
n-channel-mosfet.example: A switch-mode supply blows its fuse at switch-on. The MOSFET reads 0.1 Ω drain to source: it has failed short. Replace it and check the gate resistor and driver.
n-channel-mosfet.safety: Primary-side MOSFETs sit at mains potential: test only when isolated and discharged. Take ESD precautions.
refs: Manufacturer datasheet of the exact part number

relay.does: Switches a circuit using an electromagnet, giving isolation between control and load.
relay.principle: Current in the coil makes a magnetic field that moves an armature and closes or opens the contacts.
relay.polarity: DC relays may have a flyback diode, so the coil polarity can matter; check the datasheet.
steps: Switch off.
Measure the coil resistance and compare with the datasheet.
Check contacts at rest: COM to NC shows continuity.
Apply the rated coil voltage from a bench supply and listen for the click.
COM to NO now shows continuity.
Remove the coil voltage.
expect: Coil close to the datasheet value.
Contacts change state when the coil is energised.
faulty: Coil OL: open winding.
No click: no drive or open coil.
Contacts high resistance or stuck: burnt or welded.
relay.incircuit: With a driver and diode in circuit, readings are odd. Check the coil voltage in a powered test instead.
relay.example: A relay output does not switch. The coil sees 0 V, so the driver is at fault. If it sees 12 V with no click and the coil reads OL, replace the relay.
relay.safety: Contacts may carry mains or high current: isolate the load circuit before testing and do not touch the contact terminals.
refs: IEC 61810-1 (electromechanical elementary relays)
Manufacturer datasheet of the exact part number

fuse.does: Protects a circuit by melting when the current is too high for too long.
fuse.principle: A thin element heats with current and melts when the heating (I² × t) exceeds its rating.
apps: Over-current protection of boards and equipment
steps: Switch off and remove the fuse from its holder.
Select continuity mode or resistance.
Touch the probes to the end caps.
For glass fuses, also look at the element.
expect: Continuity, or less than a few ohms.
faulty: OL: blown.
Intermittent: poor contact in the holder.
fuse.incircuit: Test out of circuit: parallel paths can hide an open fuse.
symptoms: A new fuse that blows again points to a short
fuse.example: Replacing a blown 2 A fuse causes an immediate second blow. Do not fit a bigger fuse. Measure the resistance across the supply rail to find the short.
fuse.safety: Replace only with the same type, rating and voltage. Never bridge a fuse. Isolate before removing.
refs: IEC 60127 (miniature fuses)
Manufacturer datasheet of the exact part number

voltage-regulator.does: Provides a steady output voltage from a higher or varying input.
voltage-regulator.principle: A linear regulator drops the excess voltage as heat, P = (Vin − Vout) × I, while a feedback loop holds the output constant.
voltage-regulator.polarity: Pins are input, ground and output, and the order varies. A 7805 in TO-220 with the markings facing you is IN, GND, OUT.
steps: On a powered low-voltage board, measure the input to ground.
Measure the output to ground.
Compare both with the expected values.
Check the temperature carefully.
If the output is low, remove the load and measure again.
expect: Input at least the dropout voltage above the output (about 7 V for a 7805).
Output close to nominal within the datasheet tolerance.
faulty: Output 0 V with a good input: failed regulator or shorted load.
Output equal to input: shorted regulator.
Low output and a hot case: overloaded.
voltage-regulator.incircuit: With the power off, the resistance across the output rail shows whether the load is shorted.
voltage-regulator.example: Input 12 V, output 0.4 V and the regulator is hot. Remove the load: if the output returns to 5 V the regulator is good and the load is shorted.
voltage-regulator.safety: The regulator and heat sink get hot. Do not probe mains-side supplies.
refs: Manufacturer datasheet of the exact part number

optocoupler.does: Transfers a signal with light, keeping input and output electrically isolated.
optocoupler.principle: An LED inside lights when current flows, and a phototransistor on the other side conducts in response. The output to input current ratio is the CTR.
optocoupler.polarity: Pin 1 is marked with a dot. On a PC817, pins 1 and 2 are the LED anode and cathode, and pins 3 and 4 are the emitter and collector.
steps: Switch off and test out of circuit if possible.
Diode mode on the LED side: red on pin 1, black on pin 2.
Reverse the probes: expect OL.
The output side reads OL or high at rest.
Powered test: drive the LED with about 5 to 10 mA through a resistor and check the output transistor conducts.
expect: The LED side drops about 1.0 to 1.3 V.
The output transistor conducts when the LED is driven.
faulty: LED side open or shorted.
Output stuck on or off.
optocoupler.incircuit: In circuit, check the LED drive current (the voltage across its series resistor) and the output level in a powered test.
symptoms: A digital input that never changes
optocoupler.example: A digital input stays low. The LED side has 1.1 V across it and about 8 mA flowing, but the output stays high: the optocoupler output is faulty.
optocoupler.safety: Isolation barriers on SMPS boards carry mains-related voltages: do not probe live.
refs: Manufacturer datasheet of the exact part number

bridge-rectifier.does: Converts AC to pulsating DC using four diodes.
bridge-rectifier.principle: Two diodes conduct on each half-cycle, so current flows the same way through the load.
steps: Switch off.
Diode mode: red on an AC pin and black on +: note the drop.
Red on − and black on an AC pin: note the drop.
Reverse both: expect OL.
Between the two AC pins: expect OL both ways.
expect: About 0.5 to 0.7 V in each forward path.
OL in the reverse direction.
faulty: Low reading both ways on any pair: shorted.
OL where a forward drop is expected: open.
bridge-rectifier.incircuit: Filter capacitors and the transformer affect readings, so lift the bridge for certainty.
bridge-rectifier.example: Between + and an AC pin the meter reads 0.01 V both ways: one diode is shorted. Replace the bridge and check the filter capacitor.
bridge-rectifier.safety: Mains input: isolate and discharge first.
refs: Manufacturer datasheet of the exact part number

current-transformer-ct.does: Gives a small secondary current proportional to the primary current for metering and protection.
current-transformer-ct.principle: The primary current creates flux in the core, which induces a secondary current in the ratio of the turns: Is = Ip × (Np / Ns).
current-transformer-ct.polarity: The terminals P1, P2 (primary) and S1, S2 (secondary) show polarity. Polarity matters for directional and differential protection.
steps: Isolate and prove the primary dead, and keep the CT secondary shorted or connected to its burden as the procedure requires.
Record the nameplate: ratio, class and burden.
Measure the secondary winding resistance with a low-resistance meter.
Check the continuity of the secondary circuit and burden.
Carry out insulation, ratio and polarity tests with the approved test set and procedure.
expect: Secondary winding resistance is low and close to the datasheet or earlier record.
Continuity through the secondary circuit.
Ratio error within the accuracy class.
faulty: Open secondary circuit: dangerous when energised.
Turn-to-turn short: ratio error.
Reversed polarity.
Saturation at high current.
current-transformer-ct.incircuit: On a relay input board the CT secondary feeds burden resistors. Disconnect the relay wiring using the approved shorting arrangement before testing the CT on its own.
symptoms: Relay shows wrong or zero current
current-transformer-ct.example: A relay reads 0 A on phase B. With the primary dead, the secondary wiring is checked: continuity breaks at a loose terminal in the CT box. Re-terminate and retest.
current-transformer-ct.safety: NEVER open the secondary circuit of a CT while the primary carries current: the voltage can be dangerously high. Short the secondary with the approved link first and follow your company procedure.
refs: IEC 61869-2 (current transformers)
CT nameplate and manufacturer datasheet

voltage-transformer-vt-pt.does: Gives a small secondary voltage proportional to the primary voltage for metering and protection.
voltage-transformer-vt-pt.principle: A transformer with a high turns ratio steps the line voltage down to a standard value such as 110 V: Vs = Vp × Ns / Np.
voltage-transformer-vt-pt.polarity: Primary A, N and secondary a, n markings; correct phase connection matters.
steps: Isolate and prove the primary and secondary dead.
Record the nameplate ratio and burden.
Measure the winding resistances: the primary is much higher than the secondary.
Check the secondary fuses or MCB.
Carry out ratio and insulation tests by the approved procedure.
expect: Winding resistances consistent with records.
Ratio within the accuracy class.
faulty: Open primary or secondary.
Blown secondary fuse.
Shorted turns.
Wrong phase connection.
voltage-transformer-vt-pt.incircuit: Check the secondary fuse and wiring to the relay input first: they are the most common cause of a missing voltage.
symptoms: Relay shows no or wrong voltage
voltage-transformer-vt-pt.example: A relay shows 0 V on one phase. The VT secondary fuse is blown. After safe replacement the reading returns; find why the fuse blew, for example a shorted wire.
voltage-transformer-vt-pt.safety: Never short the secondary of a VT. Isolate the primary and secondary before work and follow the approved procedure.
refs: IEC 61869-3 (inductive voltage transformers)
Nameplate and manufacturer datasheet

tvs-diode.does: Clamps over-voltage spikes to protect circuits.
tvs-diode.principle: It conducts heavily above its breakdown voltage, sending the surge energy to ground, then recovers when the surge ends.
tvs-diode.polarity: Unidirectional types have a cathode stripe; bidirectional types have no polarity.
apps: Protecting interfaces and inputs against surges and ESD
steps: Switch off.
Diode mode: for a unidirectional part, red on the anode and black on the cathode gives the forward drop.
Reverse reads OL.
A bidirectional part reads OL both ways.
expect: Unidirectional: about 0.5 to 0.7 V forward and OL reverse.
Bidirectional: OL both ways.
faulty: Near 0 Ω both ways: shorted, the usual failure mode.
tvs-diode.incircuit: A shorted TVS pulls a rail or signal to ground. With the power off, measure the resistance to ground to find it.
tvs-diode.example: A 12 V input rail reads 0.1 Ω to ground. Removing the TVS diode makes the reading high: it failed short after a surge. Find the cause of the surge too.
tvs-diode.safety: A failed TVS may be hot.
refs: Manufacturer datasheet of the exact part number

ptc-resettable-fuse.does: Limits current by raising its resistance when it heats up, then resets when cool.
ptc-resettable-fuse.principle: A polymer PTC element has low resistance when cool. Excess current heats it, its resistance rises sharply and the current falls to a small hold value.
steps: Switch off and let the part cool.
Select the resistance range.
Measure across the part.
Compare with the datasheet cold resistance.
expect: Low resistance, typically ohms or less, when cold.
faulty: High resistance when cold: tripped or damaged.
OL: open.
ptc-resettable-fuse.incircuit: Lift one end or compare the voltage drop under normal load.
symptoms: No power on a port after an overload
ptc-resettable-fuse.example: A USB port has no output. The PTC reads 12 Ω cold, where the datasheet expects well under 1 Ω: it has failed high. Replace it after checking for the overload.
ptc-resettable-fuse.safety: It may be hot after tripping.
refs: Manufacturer datasheet of the exact part number

shunt-resistor.does: A precise low-value resistor that converts current to a small voltage for measurement.
shunt-resistor.principle: The voltage across the shunt follows V = I × R, so with a known R the current is found by measuring the drop.
shunt-resistor.polarity: No polarity. Four-terminal types have separate sense pins.
apps: Current sensing in supplies, meters and drives
steps: Switch off.
Inspect for burn marks or damage.
Use a four-wire milliohm meter for the value.
Alternatively, pass a known current and measure the small voltage across it.
expect: Close to the marked value, for example 0.01 Ω.
faulty: Open: no current reading.
Burnt or changed value: wrong current measurement.
shunt-resistor.incircuit: An ordinary multimeter cannot measure milliohms accurately. Use four-wire measurement or compare with a known good board.
shunt-resistor.example: A 0.01 Ω shunt in a charger shows 0 V across it while 5 A is flowing: the sense connection is open. Check the sense traces and solder joints.
shunt-resistor.safety: Shunts can sit at mains or bus potential: measure only with the power off or with proper isolated equipment.
refs: Manufacturer datasheet of the exact part number

terminal-block.does: Connects wires to a board or panel with a clamping screw or spring.
terminal-block.principle: A clamp presses the conductor onto a metal contact. The contact resistance should be very low.
terminal-block.polarity: No polarity, so label the pins.
apps: Field wiring of CT, VT, power and signals
steps: Switch off and isolate.
Inspect for heat marks, corrosion and loose screws.
Check continuity from the wire clamp to the PCB pin.
Check the wire strands are properly clamped.
Under authorisation, measure the voltage drop across the joint under load.
expect: Continuity with near-zero resistance.
No discolouration.
faulty: Intermittent or high resistance: loose or corroded contact.
Burn marks or a cracked housing.
terminal-block.incircuit: Use continuity or a milliohm meter with the circuit de-energised.
terminal-block.example: A relay shows an intermittent current reading. Wiggling a wire at the CT terminal block changes it: re-terminate the loose connection.
terminal-block.safety: On CT terminals do not open the circuit while energised; follow the shorting procedure. Tighten to the manufacturer torque.
refs: Manufacturer datasheet for current, voltage and torque ratings
